chapter: Hutto 1978-79: NBC, radio and the N'goma drums
title: Inventing the N'goma drums
summary: He explains naming his tuned drums N'goma from a dictionary, how they were built and tuned with a key, and that they led to his being offered a band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Okay. Now the drums that you invented, what do you call that?
G-N-O-M, Gnama or what do you say?
Yes and I got that out of a dictionary. And I went through all the drums in the dictionary to find out what the hell to call these things. And this was a
South American drum. And they used it a lot down in New Orleans and all of that stuff. And I thought that would be good for me. It sounds African, N'goma, N-G-O-M-A, N'goma.
Now did that imply a type of drums or a set of drums.

A type of drum. It was a drum this high and this big around with one head on it at the top. If you would put a head on the bottom, you wouldn't get any true tone. So you tune it with a key up here. And every day I would have to come in and tune the drum and scale-wise you know.
Now along about 1937, you had your audition band that we had. Now do you know about how much before that you invented the drums or came up with the set?
Well I don't know. It must have been, oh it must have been a good five years.
So you'd been working from 1932 or so, all during that period.
Yes. In fact, because I had the N'goma drums, this is why they wanted me as leader because it would be something different to present to the public.
